topics.cue_prompt: Describe a friend from your childhood
you_should_say: And explain what made you like him/her
topics.summary_zh: 我童年时期最好的一个朋友是吉他兴趣班的大哥哥。那是小学三年级的暑假，我报名了暑期吉他特别训练班。大哥哥是吉他班的兼职老师。在他的指导下，我的乐理知识和吉他演奏水平得到的很大的提高
topics.sample_en: A childhood friend of mine is Peter who was my guitar tutor when I was young. You know I attended a guitar class during my summer holiday when I was 10 years old. Peter worked as a part-time tutor but he could definitely play guitar at a master level(大师级). He could play all kinds of music that we like, like pop, classic, rock and so forth(等等). Peter could always give others the impression of being someone who has infinite patience(无限的耐心), like for example, he taught us playing guitar once and once again until everyone in the class got the hang of (掌握) it. Through his instructions, my level of guitar performance improved a lot. Besides music, we also had many common interests such as doing sports and playing games. So we always have something to talk about. To me, Peter is like a good listener(听众), I can talk to him about everything , especially when I am feeling down, whether it’s about my relationship, my studies or my social circle(社交圈). No one knows me better than him. He will always be there to give me encouragement and gives me constructive feedback. I am so grateful to have a close friend like Peter, someone’s always there to help me and bring me happiness, I think he is the person who made my childhood colorful and meaningful. Until now, I still keep in touch with him and we grab a drink(喝一杯) together from time to time.

p3_questions.question: What do you think of online social media?
Do you still keep in touch with your friends from childhood? Why or why not?
p3_questions.answer: Yes, I still keep in touch with my best friend from elementary school. We have known each other for 20 years. How time flies! We didn't go to the same school after graduating from elementary school, and I left our hometown when I went to college. But I would ask her out when I came home during winter or summer vacation. No matter how long we have not seen each other, whenever we get together, we still have so much to share, and we burst out laughing when we reminisce about the happy times of the past. We lead quite different lives, but I think those good memories will always connect us.

p3_questions.question: How important is childhood friendship to children?
p3_questions.answer: Childhood friendship is essential for kids. I mean, everyone needs close friends right? And this is particularly true for children. As well as bringing numerous social benefits, spending time with friends is fun and exciting for children. Friendships support children’s well-being and can help them handle different social situations. For example, by forming friendships with their contemporaries children can learn social skills like sharing and taking turns. Moreover, through interactions with friends, children learn how to negotiate, compromise, and cooperate with others. How lonely would I be if I did not have friends to play with or to talk with?

p3_questions.question: What do you think of communicating via social media?
p3_questions.answer: Well, communicating with my friends on social media has become part of my life. Sending messages back and forth to exchange our ideas and opinions is so fun and convenient, so to me, social media has become a great platform for communication. I chat with my friends on WeChat or WeBlog, and at the same time, I like to meet new friends online to grow my friendship circle. In fact, some of my online friends have also become good friends outside of social media. For this reason, I can confidently say I’m so used to communicating online that I can’t live without social media.

p3_questions.question: Do you use a lot of emojis online?
p3_questions.answer: No, I rarely use emoticons. I have to admit that in many cases emojis are a great way to break the ice, get closer to newly-met friends and present a friendly image. However, I find that collecting and finding the right emoji for a conversation is actually quite exhausting and makes communication inefficient. So gradually I started to use fewer emojis, and some of my friends laughed at me and said I didn't look like a young person at all because being skilled at using emojis is somehow a symbol of Generation Z.

p3_questions.question: Do you think online communication through social media will replace face-to-face communication?
p3_questions.answer: No, I’m afraid that I cannot agree with that. Social media does have an advantage over traditional face-to- face communication in terms of immediacy, but I think there is so much information that cannot be conveyed through the internet. For instance, the atmosphere, the tone of voice, and the subconscious micro-expressions, etc. And those are where the charm of offline communication lies. In my personal experience, since I am not good at using emojis, many of my colleagues feel that I am more serious when they talk with me online. So in my opinion, online social media will not replace face-to-face communication.

topics.cue_prompt: Describe a time when you were stuck in a traffic jam
you_should_say: And explain how you felt in the traffic jam
topics.summary_zh: 上周六我坐出租车回家，没想到正好遇到了明星来我的城市开演唱会。她的粉丝很早就到了场地，但是演唱会晚上才开始，所以她们只能在路边等场地开门。我记得那天人非常多，他们又带了横幅和一些其他的东西，造成路段非常拥堵。在车上我也不觉得无聊，反而一直照这些粉丝的照片，万一我运气好照到了这个明星了呢。所以我对这次堵车的印象不坏，我觉得我也挺开心的。
topics.sample_en: I took a taxi home last Saturday, and I didn't expect to be disrupted by the concert of a big star who was visiting my city. In fact, it's my fault that I didn't check the route in advance(提前), otherwise I wouldn't have been stuck in traffic for more than an hour. The singer's fans arrived at the venue early, but the concert didn't start until the evening, so they could only wait for the venue to open by the roadside(在路边). I remember it was very crowded that day, I think there were at least a few thousand people standing outside the venue. These enthusiastic fans brought banners and other things, such as cutouts of the celebrity (人形立牌), , which caused the road to be very congested. If I remember correctly, I even saw several police cars and ambulances parked just outside the venue. There were also several more traffic police on the road than usual. They were working hard to divert the traffic(疏导交通) and allow these fans to cross the road safely without obstructing the passage of vehicles(不要阻碍了车辆的通行). To be honest, I didn't get bored in the car. Instead, I kept taking pictures of these fans. While taking pictures, I thought, what if I was lucky enough to get a picture of this star? Wouldn't that be nice? So my impression of this traffic jam was not bad, and I think I was quite happy that day.

p3_questions.question: How can we solve the traffic jam problem?
p3_questions.answer: To solve traffic jams, I think there are several measures that need to be implemented. First, encouraging green travel to reduce the number of vehicles on the road is the primary measure to reduce traffic congestion. Public transportation and cycling are possible when travelling to a nearby place. Second, the government should introduce a reasonable set of transportation plans to help reduce traffic pressure, including road planning and vehicle restrictions. Third, a polite traffic manner can be really helpful. Many traffic jams are due to traffic accidents. Civilized driving by all can greatly reduce traffic pressure.

p3_questions.question: Do you think developing public transportation can solve traffic jam problems?
p3_questions.answer: Of course. I agree that developing public transportation can solve traffic congestion for several reasons. First, subways and buses can carry more passengers compared to cars, so using them would reduce the number of cars on the road. Second, a well-developed public transportation system will encourage citizens to use public transportation instead of driving by themselves, since public transportation is generally cheaper and more convenient. Especially when travelling to a nearby place, public transportation is a much better choice, considering the time and money spent. Third, the rising price of petrol will hopefully urge drivers to change their travel modes. A developed public transportation system should attract them.

p3_questions.question: Do you think highways can help reduce traffic jams?
p3_questions.answer: Talking about highways’ effect on reducing traffic jams, I would say it depends on the different types of highway. Ring roads are helpful because if one wants to cross the city from east to west, the ring road is the best option, because there are no traffic lights, which saves a lot of time, and they serve as a diversion for intra-city traffic. On the contrary, intercity highways barely serve this purpose. Traffic jams can be witnessed daily on intercity highways during vacations, especially the Spring Festival or May Day.

p3_questions.question: What are some effective ways to manage traffic?
p3_questions.answer: To manage traffic, the power of government and society should combine. In terms of the government, traffic laws and regulations need to be further introduced. Another solution would be to tax drivers. In London, for example, there’s a congestion charge which helps to raise money for better public transport. Public transportation also needs to be reliable and efficient, which requires government investment. In terms of society, we should reduce our dependence on cars. Workers should car share and travel together, as most tend to travel alone. Cars and roads are not used efficiently which causes traffic jams during rush hour.

p3_questions.question: Would you rather be in a car or a bus in a traffic jam?
p3_questions.answer: I would definitely choose to be in a car rather than a bus during a traffic jam. The main reason is comfort and control. In a private car, I have a comfortable seat, personal space, and the ability to adjust the air conditioning or play my own music. I can also use the time more productively — for example, making a phone call or listening to an audiobook. On a bus, I would likely have to stand in a crowded, stuffy environment with little personal space. Additionally, buses often follow fixed routes and cannot easily divert, while in a car, I could potentially use navigation apps to find an alternative route. So, a car offers a much more tolerable experience in heavy traffic.

p3_questions.question: Do you like to use public transport?
p3_questions.answer: Generally speaking, I do like using public transport, particularly the metro system. It is affordable, efficient, and environmentally friendly, since it reduces the number of private cars on the road. In Chinese cities, the subway network is extensive and well-connected, making it convenient for daily commuting. However, there are downsides. During peak hours, trains and buses become extremely crowded, and delays can happen. Also, public transport may not be as comfortable as a private car, especially when carrying heavy bags or in extreme weather. Despite these issues, I still prefer it for most trips because it saves money, reduces stress from driving, and allows me to read or listen to music during the ride.

topics.cue_prompt: Describe something that helped you learn a language
you_should_say: How it helped you learn the language
And how you felt about it
topics.summary_zh: 这是一个网站。我学习的是日语。这个网站里面除了有学习资料，还有大量的视频，不过这些都是要付费的。虽然帮助很大，但对于一个学生来说，也是一笔不小的开销。不过值得开心的是，这个网站对我日语学习提供了很大的帮助，我现在已经能和日本人进行对话了。我非常推荐这个网站，不过也希望它能降低价格，给更多人带来帮助。looking up the Japanese(大部分的人都会偷懒去阅读中文翻译，而不是查阅
topics.sample_en: I highly recommend a Japanese website to anyone learning Japanese. Because of this site, my Japanese passed the intermediate test within a year. This site is actually not entirely for free. Of course, there are some free materials on it, and many people who learn Japanese will also put some materials online. However, some of the most classic learning materials are not free of charge, but these learning materials are very effective, and the summary of knowledge points is also very comprehensive(对于知识点的总结也非常全 面). The best thing is, because this is a Japanese website, all the learning materials are in Japanese. Even if you use the website to look up words(查单 词), there are only Japanese to Japanese translations. I think this is very useful for learning languages. If it was a Chinese-Japanese translation, I believe that most people would be lazy and just go for the Chinese translation instead of 日语). In addition to learning materials, there are also a large number of learning videos on the website, but of course none of the good ones are for free. Although the website and videos helped me a lot with learning Japanese, it was also a huge expense as a student. But the good news is that I don't think the money was wasted, and the website is much cheaper than taking a training class. With the help of this Japanese site, I can now have a conversation with Japanese people. I plan to continue my Japanese studies, try to get the highest level in my Japanese test and then go to the University of Tokyo to study after graduating from university. I highly recommend this site, but I hope it will get lower in price and hence help more people.

p3_questions.question: What difficulties do people face when learning a language?
p3_questions.answer: I think people face a lot of difficulties when they learn a new language, and one of the biggest is the difference in the way we think. This may sound like it has nothing to do with learning a new language, but in fact, it is really difficult for people to truly master a foreign language if they cannot break through the problem of how people think. Take, for example, the idiomatic phrase in English: to keep your head above water. It is not actually used to describe a situation of someone struggling in water, but is used to describe a kind of predicament, especially one caused by debt, so we say “keep your head above water”. To “stay above water” is to keep yourself from falling into the quagmire of debt. So, to understand a language, you really need to understand the thinking of native speakers.

p3_questions.question: Do you think language learning is important? Why?
p3_questions.answer: Of course, language learning is very important. Simply put, language is an important tool for knowing the world. Mastering a language can open up another world for people. Do you want to know the world you didn't know? Do you want to enrich your life experience? Language can help you. From an academic point of view, languages themselves represent world views, and they can reflect their national culture and spirit through themselves. When learning a language, you can feel the charm of the language itself, you can feel its pronunciation, its text composition, the culture behind the language, and so on. On top of that, language is a skill, especially in the context of globalization, and proficiency in a foreign language can certainly enhance competitiveness in employment. Therefore, language learning is very important.

p3_questions.question: Which is better, to study alone or to study in a group? Why?
p3_questions.answer: I prefer to study alone due to the following benefits. First, there are fewer distractions. Choosing to study alone helps us focus completely on the material. We don’t have to worry about study sessions turning into hangout sessions when studying with friends. Second, we can control the study environment. Studying alone allows us to study in an environment that’s perfect for us. And the last point is that we are able to control our study schedule. Some of us work better at night; others work better during the day. When we study alone, we can plan a study schedule that works best for us and take breaks when we want. However, when students study in a group, the priority is finding a time that works for everyone, not finding a time that is most effective for studying. Studying alone allows us the freedom to choose when and how long we want to study.

p3_questions.question: What’s the best way to learn a language?
p3_questions.answer: I think the best way to learn a language is to create a “Home Immersion” situation. For example, you can use social media to immerse yourself at home or to find communities to chat with. Moreover, switching your phone’s language or watching shows in your target language will help you achieve an immersive experience, too. And of course, you’ll want as much speaking and writing practice as possible. Online tutors are one of the best ways to get great-quality speaking practice at home. In my experience, by using scientific reasoning and practicing a lot, and taking a bit of effort and patience, I believe it’s possible to create an immersive environment at home and this is an effective way to learn a language.

topics.cue_prompt: Describe a special cake you received from others
you_should_say: Who you got the cake from
And explain why it’s a special cake
topics.summary_zh: 18岁的时候正直高三最后的备考阶段，我们的班主任给我们买了一个超级大的蛋糕，纪念我们的成人礼。第一次这么多人一起吃蛋糕，而且这次成人礼真的很特别，大家也觉得特别温馨，现在想想真的很怀念当时单纯的自己。
topics.sample_en: When I turned 18 years old, it was exactly at the time of the last ! preparation phase(准备阶段)! in Grade Three of high school. Therefore, you can just imagine how busy and intense those days were. What comforted us a lot was that our head teacher bought a huge cake for us to ! commemorate(纪念)! our ! coming-of-age ceremony(成人礼)!. It was a three-layered chocolate cream cake, which could feed 40 people. It was the first time I saw such a huge cake. Looking carefully, we found our names written on the cake in extremely small and cute characters. At that moment, we truly felt our head teacher’s love for us. It was a month away from ! college entrance examination(高考)!. One day, after self-study at night was over, our head teacher and monitor placed this huge cake in front of us, saying you would experience college entrance examination soon which was a symbol of growing up, then you would enter the college and step into society and I hoped that you would be more sensible. Hearing these words, some of us couldn’t help but shed a few tears. Our head teacher cared about each of us very much, just like our parents. It was the first time for us to eat such a huge cake together with so many classmates. It was really a very special coming-of-age ceremony, warm and sweet. Looking back, I really miss that innocent and ignorant version of myself, and I really miss our head teacher and my classmates.

p3_questions.question: Do you think it’s good to communicate when eating with your family?
Why are some people willing to spend a lot of money on meals or special days?
p3_questions.answer: I think it’s because a lot of family members and relatives are together during these days and having special meals makes such events more memorable. I think festivals in general make us happier and because of the good mood, we don’t mind spending a bit extra. As for special days, let’s take an elaborate wedding as an example. Such an occasion creates memories that the couple can remember for their whole life. It is also an opportunity for young people to celebrate their happiness with their friends and family. Consequently, many people spend too much money to make it memorable and to show off their wealth and status. Moreover, such occasions give family members and friends an opportunity to get together as well.

p3_questions.question: Is there any food in your country that is eaten at special times or on special occasions?
p3_questions.answer: Yes, in my country, we have a traditional food called zongzi that is commonly eaten during special times or on special occasions. It is typically made during the Dragon Boat Festival, which falls on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. Zongzi is made by wrapping glutinous rice and various fillings, such as meat or beans, in bamboo leaves and then steaming or boiling them. The process is quite labor-intensive, but the result is a delicious and aromatic treat. This food is believed to ward off evil spirits and bring good luck. It is enjoyed by families and friends who gather together to share the joyous moment. The unique taste and cultural significance of zongzi make it a popular choice for special occasions in my country.

p3_questions.question: What are the difference between special food in China and foreign countries?
p3_questions.answer: I think the biggest difference is their ingredients. When I’m talking about foreign countries, I especially mean western counties like the United States or the UK. Special Chinese food is often made with rice. For example, the rice dumplings people eat during the Dragon Boat Festival is made with sticky rice. Another special food, tangyuan, is also made with sticky rice and stuffing, and is eaten on the Lantern Festival. Meanwhile, when looking at the US, I know that most of their special food is made with all kinds of meat and cheese. For example, American people love eating turkey on Thanksgiving, which is bird meat. Barbecue ribs are also one of the most popular things to eat in America, which is pork. I think that’s because the food culture of two groups of people differ greatly with each other.

topics.cue_prompt: Describe an important river/lake in your country
you_should_say: And explain why it is important
topics.summary_zh: 千岛湖位于浙江省杭州市。我与朋友去那里旅游时，导游曾为我们讲解过相关的知识。千岛湖面积约580平方千米，蓄水量178亿立方米。它的湖水不经任何处理即达饮用水标准，被誉为“天下第一秀水”。千岛湖是浙江省最重要的水源地之一，同时也是中国最值得一区的旅游景点之一。
topics.sample_en: Qiandao Lake is one of the biggest tourist attractions in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province. Famous for its amazing views, Qiandao Lake has also become a notable landmark of the city. When I visited it with my friends, the tour guide imparted some fascinating knowledge to us (讲解相关知识). The lake covers an area of about 600 square kilometers and has a storage capacity (立方米) of 17. 8 billion cubic meters (立方米), possessing rich natural wealth and huge economic potential. It also plays an important role in the local ecosystem, and its magnificent scenery appeals to millions of visitors every year, which brings substantial economic income to local tourism. The water of Qiandao Lake is of top-quality (优质的) among the great rivers and lakes of China. As a grade-one national water system, it reaches the criterion of healthy drinking water without needing any treatment. Therefore, it is known as the "Number One Water in the World". Qiandao Lake is also known as a rare tourist resort (罕见的旅游胜地), with 1078 islands of various shapes and sizes. Different islands harmonically exist together and form a strangely fantastic picture. It is one of the most significant water sources in Zhejiang Province, providing massive aquatic resources. At the same time, it is also one of the most scenic spots in the province and is definitely worth a visit (最值得参观的旅游景点).

p3_questions.question: How can rivers/lakes benefit local people?
p3_questions.answer: First of all, water is the source of life, providing local people with water for domestic use, industrial use and agricultural use. Because of rivers and lakes, local people have inexhaustible resources. Secondly, rivers and lakes have the function of transportation. We all know that all major cities in the world are basically located on rivers or oceans, such as New York, Hamburg, London and Sydney. The transportation facilitated by rivers allows the whole city to have better development space, and naturally, local people will benefit from it. For example, the faster the economic development of the local people, the higher their income, and the better their quality of life.

p3_questions.question: Do you think rivers/lakes attract tourists?
p3_questions.answer: Sure, I enjoy quite a few water activities. I love swimming. It burns the fat around my body, so I go swimming a lot in summer. It helps me to keep in shape (保持健康；保持好的身材)，improve my stamina (耐力) and strengthen my immune system. I also like snorkeling (浮潜) in the sea while watching colorful fish feeding (觅食) on the sea bed. Taking a ride on a speed boat (摩托艇) is not bad either, but the sea is pretty choppy (波涛汹涌的；波浪起伏的) sometimes, so it can be dangerous.

p3_questions.question: How do rivers and lakes affect local tourism?
p3_questions.answer: As I mentioned earlier, many places use their beautiful local rivers or unique lakes to attract tourists from all over the country, and even all over the world. As far as I know, one of the tributaries of the Yukon River in Canada is called the Cronk River. There is gold everywhere in this river, so this is a very famous local "money" river. For more than 100 years, people have discovered gold here, and in the next 100 years, people will continue to come here to dig for gold. Of course, some people will question whether there is actually any gold in this river, or whether it is just a myth to attract more tourists. Nevertheless, this is a perfect example of how a river or lake can affect tourism.

p3_questions.question: Are rivers and lakes good for transport?
p3_questions.answer: The answer to this question is beyond doubt. Water transportation is one of the most important modes of modern transportation. For example, about 90% of China's total import and export volume is completed on water. Water transport has many advantages over other modes of transport. First, because water routes are typically very wide, they can handle large-tonnage and long-distance transportation easily. Secondly, because waterway transportation mainly uses existing natural waterways, there is no need to build new routes like with other transportation methods, so it saves a lot of investment in laying transportation channels.

topics.cue_prompt: Describe a special day out that cost you little money/didn’t cost you much
you_should_say: And explain how you feel about the day
topics.summary_zh: 上个摄影节，我和室友一起去看在创业园区的免费摄影展，展厅非常大，而且大部分都是青年摄影师的作品。有些摄影师甚至亲自来为观展的人介绍自己的创作灵感，看到一些青年画家充满创造力的画笔，我和室友都被震撼了，虽然是免费的活动，但是我和室友在这次活动收获了很多。
topics.sample_en: Last weekend, I went out with my roommate to a photography show she found online. It was held in a start-up hub, which is not far from our campus. So we rode a public bike to the exhibition. It turned out to be an exhibition by the graduates of MA in Photojournalism from our university. The title of the exhibition was Departure. I think it suggested that it was the start of those students embracing an exciting journey into photography. The best works the students have produced in their studies, were very cutting-edge and eye-catching. What we didn’t expect was that the topics those images reflected, ranged from (从⋯到…) documenting the cultural importance of social media in Chinese universities, to the changing social landscape of immigration across China. Their photos presented a fresh perspective into our society’ s culture(全新的视角). From the unique and different photos, we felt we could already picture the photographers, a few talented youngsters who wanted to show their personality and usher their voice. On that day, I got to talk to one of the photographers and she told me all about her journey, like where she took those photos. It was quite fascinating. We were blown away (彻底震惊) by those young photographer’s great enthusiasm and talent. The admission was free and the exhibition continued until the end of the summer. When we went back, we immediately recommended the exhibition to our friends.

p3_questions.question: Do people like to spend their leisure time outside in your country?
p3_questions.answer: Some of them, yes. I know a bunch of people who can’t bear staying at home alone. Their need for social interaction is huge, so they always go out and meet people, no matter whether they are friends or strangers. But I also know some couch potatoes. The last thing they want to do is step out of their room. They’d rather have some friends come over, order some food, chat for several hours or watch a movie together. So I guess it’s really hard to tell whether people like to go out or not, because different lifestyles lead to different preferences.

p3_questions.question: How does technology affect the way people spend their leisure time?
p3_questions.answer: I think its influence on kids is the greatest. I say so because of my niece. She’s five years old and she is already a master in electronics. She lives in a high-rise building downtown, which means she basically lives in a concrete jungle. Both of her parents are busy with work, so they barely take her out into nature, or anywhere far away from the city. As a result, she knows how to cut a watermelon on an iPad, but she doesn’t know that watermelons grow in the land, not on trees. As for adults, I’d say technology makes things easier. For example, to buy a film ticket, all you need to do is download an app and make a few clicks with your finger.

p3_questions.question: Do you think only old people have time for leisure?
p3_questions.answer: It sounds a little bit sad, but I think it’s true. Young people in China just don’t have the time for recreation. They have too many things to worry about such as employment, housing, marriage, kids - the list goes on. I don’t know whether it’s the same in other countries, but the young generation in China don’t have the time to enjoy themselves, nor are they ever in the mood for leisure activities. Things are totally different for old people. They’ve got time and money, so as long as they want to, they can have as much fun as possible.

p3_questions.question: Going out to have holidays is tiring. Why do people still want to do it?
p3_questions.answer: Even though going on holiday can be physically tiring, people still choose to do it because the benefits usually outweigh the discomfort. Traveling allows people to break out of their daily routines and experience something new, whether it’s a different culture, scenery, or food. This kind of novelty can be very refreshing mentally. In addition, holidays often create lasting memories with family or friends, which are more valuable than a few days of rest at home. For many people, the tiredness is temporary, but the joy and relaxation they gain can last much longer. That’s why they are willing to put up with the exhaustion.

p3_questions.question: Why do people like to have days off?
p3_questions.answer: People like to have days off mainly because it allows them to take a break from their daily routines. Modern life is quite stressful, especially for students and office workers who have to face tight deadlines and heavy workloads. Having a day off gives them a chance to relax, sleep in, and recover their energy. It also provides time to spend with family and friends, or to focus on personal hobbies that they normally don’t have time for. From a psychological perspective, taking regular breaks can prevent burnout and improve overall happiness. That’s why people really look forward to their days off.

p3_questions.question: How do people spend their leisure time in your country?
p3_questions.answer: In my country, people spend their leisure time in various ways depending on their age and interests. Young people often enjoy scrolling through short videos on their phones, playing online games with friends, or going to shopping malls and cafés. Middle-aged and older adults prefer calmer activities like walking in the park, doing Tai Chi, or gathering together for square dancing. On weekends and holidays, many families go on short trips, watch movies, or have big meals together. Recently, new forms of leisure like camping, hiking, and script-based role-playing games have also become very popular among young people.

topics.cue_prompt: Describe an environmental law you would like your country to introduce
you_should_say: Why people should follow the law
Whether the law will be popular
And explain how you feel about this law
topics.summary_zh: 提议立法：全国禁止生产和销售一次性塑料吸管（医疗和残疾等特殊需要除外）。塑料吸管是海洋垃圾前十名，无法有效回收，海洋动物误食。奶茶爱好者可能抱怨纸吸管软，但已有金属和硅胶吸管替代。我看过海龟被吸管塞住鼻孔的视频，心都碎了。我自己已经一年没用塑料吸管，很简单。14亿人如果都这样，就能从环境中移除几十亿根吸管。
topics.sample_en: I want to propose a very specific but impactful law: a nationwide ban on the production and use of single-use plastic straws. There would be exceptions for medical需要使用 and for people with disabilities, but for everyday drinks like milk tea, bottled water, and soft drinks, plastic straws would be illegal. What would the law be? The law would take effect one year after passage, giving businesses time to switch to alternatives like paper straws, bamboo straws, or reusable silicone straws. Fast food chains and bubble tea shops would be required to offer straws only upon request, not automatically. Violators would face increasing fines. Why should people follow it? Because plastic straws are among the top ten items found in ocean cleanups. They are too small and light to be recycled efficiently, so most end up in landfills or the ocean. Marine animals mistake them for food. And let’s be honest – most of us don’t actually need a straw to drink. It’s a convenience we have normalised. Will it be popular? Among environmentalists and young people, yes. But bubble tea fans might complain that paper straws get soggy. The key is to encourage better alternatives – there are now reusable metal and silicone straws that work perfectly. The law would need a public education campaign to explain why the change is necessary. How do I feel about this law? I feel strongly positive. I’ve seen videos of sea turtles with straws stuck in their noses. It’s heartbreaking. Such a small change in our daily habits – simply not using a straw – can have a huge impact. I’ve already stopped using plastic straws for a year. It was easy. If a billion people did the same, we would remove billions of straws from the environment. This law is a no-brainer.

p3_questions.question: Will there be a law that is universally accepted?
p3_questions.answer: While complete universal acceptance of a single law is highly unlikely given cultural, religious, and political diversity, certain legal principles have achieved near‑universal recognition. For example, prohibitions against genocide, torture, slavery, and piracy are accepted by nearly all nations, often through international treaties like the Geneva Conventions or UN declarations. However, even these face occasional violations or differing interpretations. Laws concerning more subjective matters — such as drug policy, free speech limits, or family law — vary widely. The closest we might come is a framework of shared fundamental human rights, but full universality remains an ideal rather than a reality. Ultimately, respect for national sovereignty makes universally accepted law improbable.

p3_questions.question: What kinds of rules do schools in China have?
p3_questions.answer: Chinese schools typically have a comprehensive set of rules covering multiple areas. Academic rules require students to complete assignments, attend classes punctually, and maintain academic integrity during exams. Behavioral rules emphasize respect for teachers,禁止 fighting or bullying, and following classroom discipline. Dress codes are common — many schools mandate uniforms and restrict hairstyles, jewelry, and makeup. Technology rules strictly limit smartphone use during class, and some schools ban phones entirely on campus. Attendance rules require students to provide valid reasons for absences. Safety rules include fire drills and restrictions on leaving campus during school hours. These rules aim to create a disciplined, focused, and safe learning environment.

p3_questions.question: How does technology affect the law?
p3_questions.answer: Technology profoundly affects the law in several ways. On one hand, it creates new legal challenges — cybercrime, data privacy breaches, AI accountability, and intellectual property issues in the digital space require constantly updated laws and regulations. On the other hand, technology improves legal processes. For example, e‑courts, digital case management, and AI‑powered legal research make the justice system faster and more transparent. Technology also enables better law enforcement through surveillance tools and data analysis. However, it can also outpace existing laws, creating gaps. Legislators must continually adapt, balancing innovation with protection of citizens' rights. Ultimately, technology forces the law to evolve more quickly than ever before.

topics.cue_prompt: Describe a time when a person did something tohelp you solve a problem
you_should_say: And explain how you felt about the experience
topics.summary_zh: 猫从阳台门溜走，找了两小时没找到，在楼道哭。70多岁退休邻居刘大爷看见，拿了手电筒找车底、排水管、垃圾桶后。40分钟后在停车场角落车底找到发抖的猫。给钱不收，说“我退休了没事干”。感受到社区里陌生人的善意。现在每年春节给他烤饼干。
topics.sample_en: I’d like to talk about how a retired neighbour helped me find my cat. My cat, Dou Dou, is an indoor cat. One evening, I left the balcony door open for five minutes. He slipped out. I didn’t notice until two hours later. I was terrified. Dou Dou had never been outside. What was the problem? I searched the whole building. I went up and down the stairs 10 times. I checked every corner of the compound. Nothing. It was dark. I was crying. I put up “Lost Cat” signs, but I had no hope. How did a person help me? My neighbour, Uncle Liu, a retired factory worker in his 70s, saw me crying in the hallway. He asked what happened. Then he said, “Cats don’t go far. They get scared and hide.” He took a flashlight and started checking places I hadn’t thought of – under parked cars, inside drainage pipes, behind trash bins. He also called Dou Dou’s name in a low, gentle voice, not loud shouting. After 40 minutes, he found Dou Dou hiding under a car in the far corner of the parking lot. The cat was shaking. Uncle Liu picked him up carefully and handed him to me. He said, “Next time, keep the door closed.” How did I feel? I felt like I had just won the lottery. I offered Uncle Liu money. He refused. He said, “I’m retired. I have nothing to do anyway.” That night, I learned that communities are built on small kindnesses from people you barely know. Uncle Liu didn’t have to help. But he did. I bake him cookies now every Chinese New Year.

p3_questions.question: How important is it for schools to help children pecome smarter?
p3_questions.answer: It is quite important for schools to help children become smarter, but it depends on how we define "smarter." If it means improving academic abilities like logic, reading, and problem-solving, then schools play a central role because that is their main purpose. However, being smart also includes emotional intelligence, creativity, and social skills. Schools should focus not only on test scores but also on helping children think critically and learn how to learn. That said, families and life experiences are equally important. Schools alone cannot make a child smart; they need to work together with parents and the wider environment.

topics.cue_prompt: Describe a story/book with animals in it
you_should_say: And explain what you think of this story/book
topics.summary_zh: 我要介绍的是安娜·塞维尔的《黑骏马》。主角是一匹叫黑骏马的黑马，故事是从马的角度讲的。故事讲的是黑骏马的一生。他一开始在一个好农场里很快乐，但后来被卖给不同的主人。有些主人善良，有些很残忍，让他拉重车、打他、让他住得很差。他受了很多苦。但最后他被卖给了一位善良的主人。我是13岁左右读这本书的。我觉得这本书非常重要。它不仅是关于一匹马的故事，更是关于动物福利的书。作者写这本书就是为了改变人们对待马的方式。这本书悲伤但有希望，它教会我们对动物要有同理心。
topics.sample_en: I want to describe a book with animals in it. The book is Black Beauty by Anna Sewell. It was published in 1877 and is one of the most famous animal books in English literature. The main animal in this book is Black Beauty, a black horse. The story is told from the horse's point of view. There are also other horses like Ginger and Merrylegs, as well as dogs and other animals. The story is about Black Beauty's life. He starts as a happy young horse on a nice farm with kind owners. But over time, he is sold to different owners. Some owners are kind, but some are very cruel. They make him pull heavy carriages, beat him, and put him in bad conditions. He suffers a lot. But in the end, he is sold to a kind owner who gives him a good home. The book was written to show how badly horses were treated in Victorian England. I read this book when I was about 13. My aunt gave it to me as a birthday present because she knew I loved horses. I remember crying several times while reading it. I think this book is very important. It is not just a story about a horse. It is a book about animal welfare. The author wrote it to change how people treat horses. Because of this book, many people became more aware of animal suffering. Laws in England were changed to protect horses. The book is sad but hopeful. It teaches empathy for animals. It also shows that one book can make a real difference in the world. That is why I admire Black Beauty.

p3_questions.question: Why do people always tell children stories with animals?
p3_questions.answer: People tell children stories with animals because children naturally love animals. Animals are interesting to children. They are different from humans, so they capture a child's imagination. A child might not care about a story about a man going to work, but they will listen to a story about a rabbit going on an adventure. Also, animal stories are safe. If you tell a story about a bad child, the child might feel attacked. But if you tell a story about a bad wolf, the child understands the lesson without feeling personally blamed. Animals create distance. This distance makes it easier for children to learn about right and wrong without feeling judged.

p3_questions.question: What are the advantages of keeping a pet?
p3_questions.answer: There are many advantages to keeping a pet. First, pets provide companionship. If you live alone or feel lonely, a pet can be a good friend. They are always there for you. Second, pets can improve your physical health. Dog owners have to walk their dogs every day, which is good exercise. Studies show that people with pets have lower blood pressure and less stress. Third, pets teach responsibility, especially for children. When a child helps feed and care for a pet, they learn that other living things depend on them. This helps children become more mature and caring. So pets are good for both mental and physical health.

p3_questions.question: Do many people keep pets in your country?
p3_questions.answer: Yes, more and more people in China keep pets now. In the past, most families did not have pets because people were poor and apartments were small. But in the last ten or fifteen years, the middle class has grown. People have more money and bigger homes. Now, especially in big cities like Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou, many people have dogs or cats. Small dog breeds like Poodles and Pomeranians are very popular. Cats have also become more popular because they are cleaner and need less space. Some people keep fish, birds, or hamsters. The pet industry in China is huge. There are pet hotels, pet spas, and even pet birthday cakes.

p3_questions.question: Many people regard pets as members of thei family. What do you think?
p3_questions.answer: I think it is completely natural to regard pets as family members. People spend years living with their pets. They feed them, clean up after them, take them to the vet when they are sick, and play with them every day. That sounds like family to me. Also, pets give unconditional love. They don't care if you are rich or poor, beautiful or plain. They are always happy to see you. In return, people love them deeply. When a pet dies, many people grieve just as they would for a human family member. I don't think there is anything wrong with this. It shows that humans are capable of love beyond our own species.

p3_questions.question: Some people think pets should not be kept in cities. What do you think?
p3_questions.answer: I understand why some people think pets should not be in cities, but I don't fully agree. It is true that cities are not ideal for some animals. For example, large dogs need space to run, and city apartments may not be enough. Also, city noise and crowds can stress animals. However, many pets are fine in cities. Cats are often happy indoors. Small dog breeds can get enough exercise in a small apartment if walked properly. Instead of banning pets, cities should have better rules. For example, limit the size of dogs in apartments. Provide more dog parks. Fine owners who don't clean up. A complete ban is too extreme.

p3_questions.question: Should schools teach children about animals?
p3_questions.answer: Of course schools should teach children about animals, but not just in science class. Animals can be used to teach many subjects. For example, stories about animals can teach moral lessons in literature class. The tortoise and the hare teaches about perseverance. In art class, children can draw or paint animals. This helps them observe carefully. In math class, you can use animals to make word problems more interesting, like "If a cat has four kittens and each kitten drinks 50ml of milk a day, how much milk do they drink?" Learning about animals also teaches responsibility. If a class has a pet, children learn to feed and care for it. This is a very practical life skill.

topics.name_zh: 很久没收到回复的信息
topics.cue_prompt: Describe a time when you sent a message or anemail to someone but received no reply for a longtime
you_should_say: Whether you finally received the reply
And explain how you felt about the experience
topics.summary_zh: 租的房子空调坏了，38度天。给房东发微信报修，周一发已读不回。周二再发，已读不回。周三打电话说“我问问”。周五第三次发，周六回“修理工明天来”。六天才修好。愤怒——她每天看到消息但不回，哪怕说“在找了”也好。沉默让我觉得她不在乎我受罪。合同到期就搬走。学会紧急事项要书面记录、要时间表。
topics.sample_en: I want to describe a practical message that went unanswered. Last summer, the air conditioner in my rented apartment broke down. It was July, and the temperature in my city reached 38 degrees Celsius. Sleeping was impossible. I was sweating through my shirts at home. What was the message about? I sent a WeChat message to my landlord. I wrote: “Hello, Auntie Zhang. The AC isn’t working. It blows air but no cold air. Could you please send someone to fix it? It’s very hot. Thank you.” I sent it on a Monday morning. She read it at 9 AM. No reply. I sent a follow-up on Tuesday: “Just a reminder about the AC.” Read, no reply. Wednesday: I called her. She said, “I’ll ask someone.” Thursday: nothing. Friday: I sent a third message, more direct: “I can’t sleep at night. Please help.” She replied on Saturday: “Repairman will come tomorrow.”. Did I finally receive a reply? Yes, but after six days. The repairman came on Sunday. He said the coolant was empty. He filled it. The AC worked. How did I feel? I was angry. She saw my messages every day but chose not to reply. A simple “I’m looking for someone” would have helped. The silence made me feel like she didn’t care about my suffering. After that, I moved out as soon as my lease ended. I also learned to put urgent requests in writing and to document everything. Now I always ask for a timeline when I report a problem.

p3_questions.question: How do you show your respect in your messages?
p3_questions.answer: Showing respect in written messages involves several practices. I always begin with an appropriate greeting, such as "Hello" or "Dear [name]", and end with a polite closing like "Best regards" or "Thanks". I use respectful language — "please", "thank you", "I appreciate" — and avoid overly casual abbreviations or slang, especially with elders or superiors. I proofread my messages to ensure clarity and a polite tone. Responding in a timely manner also shows respect; if I cannot reply immediately, I acknowledge the message and say when I will respond. Additionally, I avoid interrupting or sending multiple follow‑ups impatiently. Using the recipient's correct title or name further demonstrates attention and respect.

p3_questions.question: Why do some people prefer sending a messageinstead of making a call?
p3_questions.answer: There are several reasons people prefer messaging over calling. First, messaging is asynchronous — it allows both parties to respond at their own convenience, without interrupting each other's activities. Second, it gives people time to formulate thoughtful replies, which is especially useful for sensitive or complex topics. Third, messaging reduces social pressure; introverts or those with social anxiety often find calls stressful. Fourth, written messages create a permanent record, which helps with remembering details or clarifying misunderstandings later. Finally, messaging is more efficient for simple questions or quick updates, and it works well in noisy environments or places where calls are inappropriate, such as libraries or open offices.

p3_questions.question: What would you do if you did not receive a reply after sending out a message?
p3_questions.answer: My response depends on the urgency and importance of the message. For non‑urgent social messages, I usually wait a day or two, understanding that the person may be busy or distracted. If I still need a reply, I send a polite follow‑up — something like, "Have you had a chance to think about this?" For time‑sensitive or professional matters, I might wait a few hours, then send a gentle reminder. If the issue is critical and I receive no reply after two attempts, I would switch to another channel, such as a phone call or email. I avoid sending repeated messages in quick succession, as that can appear pushy or anxious.

p3_questions.question: In what situations do people not respond to messages at all?
p3_questions.answer: People may completely ignore messages in several situations. Obvious spam, promotional texts, or messages from unknown numbers are frequently deleted without a reply. If a message is aggressive, disrespectful, or emotionally draining, recipients may choose not to engage. Another common case is when a reply is unnecessary — for example, a simple confirmation like "Got it" or a message that concludes a conversation. Additionally, people going through personal difficulties or social burnout might temporarily withdraw from all communication. In professional contexts, some messages are intentionally left unread if they fall outside the recipient's responsibilities. However, consistently ignoring important messages from friends or colleagues is generally considered rude.

p3_questions.question: In what situations do people spend a long time responding to others' messages?
p3_questions.answer: There are several common situations where people take a long time to respond. First, during work hours, meetings, or classes, people may be unable to check their phones due to professional or academic obligations. Second, when a message requires emotional or thoughtful input — such as a sensitive question or a request for serious advice — people often delay replying until they can formulate a proper response. Third, some individuals experience notification overload and simply forget to reply after reading a message. Finally, introverts or people feeling stressed might need time to mentally prepare before responding. In these cases, a delayed reply is rarely intentional rudeness.

topics.cue_prompt: Describe a time when you organized a happy eventsuccessfully
you_should_say: Who helped you to organize it
And explain why you think it was a successful event
topics.summary_zh: 为内向朋友小陈办生日，他不喜欢被关注。我只请了三个人的迷你派对：他、我、另一个朋友。主题是他爱的东西：桌游、炸鸡、日本动漫电影。借了投影仪，学做了炸鸡，买了个小芝士蛋糕插一根蜡烛。他看见蛋糕说“哦？我生日？我都忘了”，笑了（不是礼貌笑，是真笑）。他说“谢谢你没搞大场面”。成功因为尊重他的性格。大派对会让他痛苦，小派对让他快乐。派对的目标是客人开心，不是人多。
topics.sample_en: I’d like to describe a birthday party I organised for a close friend who hates big gatherings. My friend Xiao Chen is very introverted. The thought of being the centre of attention at a large party makes him physically uncomfortable. Past birthdays, he just pretended nothing was happening. What was the event? I organised a “mini party” with only three people: me, Xiao Chen, and our mutual friend Xiao Liu. The theme was “things Xiao Chen loves”: board games, his favourite fried chicken, and watching a Japanese anime movie. How did I prepare? First, I chose a date when Xiao Chen had no classes. I told him we were just having a casual dinner – no mention of birthday. Second, I bought a small cake – not a big birthday cake, just a small cheesecake. I put a single candle on it. Third, I borrowed a projector from the student union so we could watch the anime on a big wall. Fourth, I learned to cook his favourite fried chicken recipe from online videos. Who helped me? Xiao Liu helped me set up the projector and bought the drinks. Xiao Chen’s roommate helped me keep him away from the dorm while we set up. Why was it successful? Because Xiao Chen was genuinely surprised and comfortable. When he saw the small cake, he said, “Oh, it’s my birthday? I forgot.” He smiled – a real smile, not the polite one. We ate, played board games, and watched the movie until 2 AM. He told me later, “Thank you for not making it a big deal.” The event was successful because I respected who he is. A big party would have made him miserable. A small, personal event made him happy. The goal of a party is the happiness of the guest, not the size of the crowd.

p3_questions.question: Do you prefer to prepare and organize an activity or just take part in an activity?
p3_questions.answer: It depends on the type of activity and my relationship with the other people involved. For casual social events, like a weekend barbecue with close friends, I prefer to just participate and relax. Organising can add unnecessary pressure. However, for activities where I have specific ideas or a strong interest in the outcome — such as a group travel plan or a study group — I actually enjoy taking a lead role in organising. I find satisfaction in creating a smooth plan and seeing others enjoy it. That said, organising large or formal events can be exhausting, so I might prefer to participate unless I'm specifically responsible. Ultimately, a balance of both roles is ideal.

p3_questions.question: How would you feel when you were not well prepared for something?
p3_questions.answer: Being unprepared for something important typically triggers a mix of negative emotions. I often feel anxiety and stress, as uncertainty about the outcome increases. There is also a sense of regret — wishing I had started earlier or managed my time better. In social or professional settings, embarrassment may arise if others notice my lack of preparation. Physically, I might experience a racing heartbeat, sweating, or difficulty concentrating. However, mild unpreparedness for low‑stakes situations, like a casual meeting, might only cause slight discomfort. Over time, I've learned that these feelings serve as useful feedback. They motivate me to improve my planning and time management for future tasks.

p3_questions.question: Do people need others' help when organizing things?
p3_questions.answer: Whether people need help with organisation depends on the scale and complexity of the task. For personal, routine matters — like planning a daily schedule or packing for a short trip — most people can manage independently. However, for larger or unfamiliar tasks — such as organising a major family event, coordinating a work project, or moving to another city — others' help is often valuable. Different people bring different strengths, such as budgeting, design, or time management. Collaboration can also reduce oversight and stress. Additionally, asking for advice from someone who has organised a similar event can save time and prevent mistakes. So, while self‑organisation is a useful skill, knowing when to seek help is equally important.

p3_questions.question: Does everything need to be well prepared?
p3_questions.answer: Not everything requires meticulous preparation. High‑stakes situations — such as university entrance exams, job interviews, medical procedures, or business presentations — clearly benefit from thorough preparation. However, over‑preparing for minor, routine activities, like a casual coffee with friends or a daily commute, can cause unnecessary stress and waste time. Moreover, some of life's best moments come from spontaneity — an unplanned trip or a sudden opportunity. Complete preparation can also reduce flexibility and creativity. The key is to assess the importance and potential consequences of each situation. For critical events, prepare well; for low‑risk, everyday matters, a general outline or even an open mind is sufficient.

p3_questions.question: On what occasions do people need to be organized?
p3_questions.answer: Organisational skills are essential in many situations. Academic settings demand organisation — for example, managing multiple assignments, exam preparation, or group projects. In the workplace, meeting tight deadlines, handling several clients, or leading a team project require careful planning. Life events such as moving to a new house, wedding planning, or international travel also demand high levels of organisation. Even daily routines like meal planning, budgeting, or balancing work and family responsibilities benefit from being organised. Essentially, any situation with multiple tasks, limited time, or important consequences calls for organisation. Without it, people risk missing deadlines, forgetting key details, or feeling overwhelmed.

p3_questions.question: How can parents help children to be organized?
p3_questions.answer: Parents can foster organisational skills in children through several practical strategies. Establishing consistent daily routines — for meals, homework, and bedtime — helps children understand time management. Providing tools like colour‑coded folders for different subjects or a wall calendar for deadlines teaches them to track responsibilities. Parents can also involve children in planning, such as packing school bags the night before or preparing for a family trip together. Modelling organised behaviour is crucial; if parents keep their own spaces tidy and follow schedules, children naturally imitate. Praise and positive reinforcement when children complete tasks independently encourage continued effort. Over time, these habits become automatic, building a foundation for self‑discipline.

topics.cue_prompt: Describe a long-term goal/ambition you would like to achieve
you_should_say: How long you have had this goal/ambition
And explain why you set it
topics.summary_zh: 想完成一次全程马拉松，这个目标已有两年。不求速度，只求在官方时限内完赛。按计划训练：5公里、10公里、半马、全马。每周跑三次，即使冷或下雨。加入跑团互相激励。设置这个目标是为了证明自己能坚持做一件难事。学生时代我什么事都半途而废，马拉松训练需要持续数年。已完成的长跑让我在精神上也变强了。
topics.sample_en: I’d like to describe a physical goal that I’ve been working towards for two years: to complete a full marathon, which is 42. 195 kilometres. I’ve always admired marathon runners, but I never thought I could be one. I was the kid who always finished last in school races. What is the goal? To finish, not to win. I want to run a certified marathon – maybe the Shanghai Marathon or the Xiamen Marathon – within the official time limit (usually 6 hours). I don’t care about my speed. I just want to cross that finish line. How will I achieve it? I’m following a structured training plan. I started with 5K runs two years ago. Then I did a 10K race last year. This year, I’m training for a half marathon. Next year, I’ll start full marathon training. I run three times a week, even when it’s cold or raining. I also do strength training to protect my knees. I keep a training log to track my progress. I’ve joined a local running group – they motivate me when I want to quit. Why did I set this goal? Because I want to prove to myself that I can do something hard that takes a long time. In school, I was average at everything. I never stuck with anything long enough to become good. Marathon training requires consistency for years. It’s not about talent – it’s about showing up. Every time I finish a long run, I feel stronger mentally, not just physically. This goal has already changed how I approach other challenges. If I can run 30 kilometres, I can probably finish that difficult project at work too.

p3_questions.question: What should people do to achieve their goals?
p3_questions.answer: Achieving goals requires a combination of planning, discipline, and adaptability. First, set specific, measurable, and realistic goals — vague dreams like "get fit" are less effective than "go to the gym three times a week". Then, break large goals into manageable steps and create a timeline. Consistent effort is key; even small daily actions add up over time. It's also important to track progress and celebrate small wins to stay motivated. When obstacles appear, successful people adjust their strategies rather than giving up. Seeking mentorship or learning from others who have achieved similar goals can provide useful shortcuts. Finally, maintaining a positive mindset and learning from failures, rather than fearing them, makes the journey sustainable.

p3_questions.question: What goals do young people usually have?
p3_questions.answer: Young people's goals vary, but several are nearly universal. Education and career goals dominate — doing well in school, entering a respected university, or landing a promising job. Financial goals such as saving for a house, a car, or starting a business are also common. Many young people seek personal development, including learning new languages, acquiring technical skills, or improving physical fitness. Travel and cultural exploration have become increasingly popular goals, especially among those who value experiences over material possessions. Additionally, some young people aim to build meaningful relationships or contribute to society through volunteering. While priorities differ, most young people strive for a combination of stability, growth, and enjoyment.

p3_questions.question: Is it necessary to give advice to children?
p3_questions.answer: Giving advice to children is certainly necessary, but the approach matters greatly. Young children lack the cognitive maturity to foresee consequences, so adult guidance helps them navigate safety, social behaviour, and basic decision-making. For example, advice about road safety or respecting others is essential. However, as children grow older, advice should become less directive and more supportive. Over-advising can prevent children from developing critical thinking and independence. The best strategy is to offer advice when asked or when safety is at risk, but also allow children to experience natural consequences from minor mistakes. Balanced guidance helps children learn while building confidence and problem-solving skills.

p3_questions.question: What goals do people at your age have?
p3_questions.answer: For people in their twenties in China, common goals revolve around career development, financial independence, and personal growth. Many aim to secure a stable job with good prospects, often in competitive industries like technology, finance, or education. Financial goals include saving for a down payment on a house — a major milestone in Chinese culture — or building an emergency fund. Others focus on further education, such as a master's degree or professional certifications. Health and work-life balance have also become increasingly important, so goals like regular exercise or learning to cook appear frequently. Additionally, some seek meaningful relationships or travel experiences. Overall, stability and self-improvement are central themes.

p3_questions.question: Do people need to have goals?
p3_questions.answer: Yes, having goals is essential for most people. Goals provide a sense of purpose and direction, helping individuals prioritise their time and energy. They also serve as a source of motivation; when people work towards something meaningful, they are more likely to persist through difficulties. Moreover, achieving goals boosts self-esteem and life satisfaction. Even small, short-term goals — like exercising three times a week — can create positive habits. That said, goals should be realistic and flexible. Unrealistic or overly rigid goals can lead to frustration. So while goals are not absolutely necessary for survival, they greatly enhance personal growth, productivity, and overall well-being.

p3_questions.question: What goals should a society have?
p3_questions.answer: A society should pursue a balanced set of goals. Economic goals include providing stable employment, reducing poverty, and fostering innovation. Social goals involve ensuring access to quality education, affordable healthcare, and social justice for all citizens regardless of gender, ethnicity, or background. Environmental goals are equally important — reducing pollution, protecting natural resources, and addressing climate change. Additionally, a society should promote safety, political stability, and cultural development, allowing people to express themselves freely. Ultimately, the ultimate goal is to improve the overall well-being and happiness of its citizens, not just material wealth. Achieving these requires cooperation between government, businesses, and individuals.

topics.cue_prompt: Describe a person who met difficulties but succeeded
you_should_say: And explain how you feel about him
topics.summary_zh: 高中同学小王，家境极穷：父亲残疾，母亲卖菜，住一间房，没书桌，晚上点煤油灯学习。每天走5公里上学省车费。很多人说“穷孩子当不了教授”。他高考全省前100名，拿全奖读本科，又读清华博士。我为他骄傲也自愧不如。他的成功不是运气，是12年不间断的努力。每想放弃就想他，他连煤油灯都能克服，我有什么不能？
topics.sample_en: I want to describe a former classmate of mine, let’s call him Xiao Wang. We went to the same high school in a small town. He is now a PhD student at Tsinghua University, one of China’s top schools. But getting there was not easy. What difficulties did he meet? Xiao Wang’s family was very poor. His father was disabled and couldn’t work. His mother sold vegetables at the market. They lived in a one-room house with no proper desk. Xiao Wang studied on a small wooden box by the window. At night, he used a kerosene lamp because the electricity was often cut. Many people in our town thought he was wasting his time – “poor kids don’t become professors,” they said. How did he overcome them? He simply refused to give up. He woke up at 5 AM every day to study before school. He borrowed textbooks from older students because he couldn’t afford new ones. He walked 5 kilometres to school every day to save bus fare. In the national college entrance exam, he scored among the top 100 in our province. He got a full scholarship for university and then another for his PhD. How do I feel about him? I feel both proud and humbled. I knew him personally, so I know his success wasn’t luck. It was 12 years of relentless effort. When I feel like giving up on something, I think of Xiao Wang studying by kerosene lamp. If he could overcome poverty, poor facilities, and doubt from others, I can overcome my small problems. He is my definition of perseverance.

p3_questions.question: In your country, what industry is it easier to besuccessful in?
p3_questions.answer: In China, the technology and e-commerce sectors are often seen as industries where success is more attainable, especially for young entrepreneurs. Platforms like Taobao, JD. com, and Douyin (TikTok) allow individuals to start online stores with relatively low startup costs. Live-stream selling and social commerce have also created new opportunities. Additionally, the food delivery and logistics industry has grown rapidly, with companies like Meituan and Ele. me offering flexible work. That said, success in any industry requires hard work, market understanding, and a bit of luck. Traditional industries like manufacturing or state-owned sectors may offer stability but require more capital or connections. So for young people with limited resources, the internet-based economy provides the clearest path.

topics.cue_prompt: Describe a time when you changed an important opinion of yours
you_should_say: And explain how you felt about the experience
topics.summary_zh: 受父母影响，认为男人必须买房才能结婚，否则就是不负责、不稳。哥哥没买房就结婚了，租房住市中心。他说首付会耗尽积蓄加上三十年房贷，那会限制职业选择——不敢换低薪但喜欢的工作、不敢创业。两年后他们为更好的工作搬了两次家，旅行、存钱、看起来自由快乐。我改变看法：有房好，没房不代表失败。灵活性和追求机会的自由可能比固定资产更有价值。感觉压力小了，不再把房子当结婚前提。
topics.sample_en: I want to describe an opinion change about marriage and housing. My original opinion was very traditional and strongly influenced by my parents: a man must own a home before getting married. Without a house, you cannot provide stability for your family. I thought renting was wasteful, unstable, and a sign of failure. This opinion started to change when my older brother got married without buying an apartment. He and his wife rented a small place in the city centre. My parents were angry and worried. But my brother explained his reasoning: the down payment for a house would cost all his savings plus a thirty-year mortgage. That mortgage would limit his career choices – he couldn’t take a lower-paying but more meaningful job. He couldn’t start a business. Renting gave him flexibility. I watched them over the next two years. They moved twice for better jobs. They travelled. They saved money. They seemed happy and free. I started to question my original belief. I changed my opinion: owning a home is good, but not owning one is not a failure. Flexibility and freedom to pursue opportunities can be more valuable than a fixed asset. How do I feel? Less pressured. I no longer see a house as a prerequisite for marriage. My parents still disagree, but I feel clearer about my own values. This change felt like growing up.

p3_questions.question: Do children communicate more with teachers orwith parents?
p3_questions.answer: Generally, children communicate more frequently with parents than with teachers, simply due to the amount of time spent together. Young children talk to parents throughout the day about daily routines, emotions, and school experiences. With teachers, interactions are mainly confined to school hours and focused on academic instruction, classroom behaviour, or group activities. However, communication patterns shift as children grow. Teenagers may talk less to parents about certain issues and more to teachers, especially regarding academic advice, future plans, or subject interests. Also, children who board at school might have more communication with teachers. Nevertheless, for most children in regular day schools, parents remain the primary and most frequent communication partners.

p3_questions.question: Whose opinions are more important to children,their parents or teachers?
p3_questions.answer: The relative importance of parents' versus teachers' opinions changes as children develop. For preschoolers and early primary students, parents' opinions are usually more influential because parents provide emotional security, basic values, and daily guidance. Teachers become increasingly important around ages 7 to 12, especially on academic matters, social behaviour in school, and fairness. Children often seek teachers' approval for school-related tasks and peer conflicts. During adolescence, peer opinions often overtake both, but parents and teachers still matter on different issues — parents for long- term life decisions, teachers for academic and career advice. So neither is universally more important; it depends on the child's age and the context.

p3_questions.question: When do most children begin to have their ownopinions?
p3_questions.answer: Children typically begin expressing their own opinions around the age of two to three, when language skills develop enough to state preferences like "I want milk" or "I don't like this". However, these early opinions are mostly about concrete likes and dislikes. By ages five to seven, children can form and defend simple opinions on fairness, friendship, or rules, based on their own reasoning. During adolescence, opinions become more abstract and independent, covering areas like values, social issues, and personal identity. The development of opinions is gradual and influenced by family, school, and peers, but the foundation appears in early childhood.

topics.cue_prompt: Describe a food that people eat on special occasions/events
you_should_say: And explain why people eat it on that special occasion/event
topics.summary_zh: 我要介绍的是月饼，人们在中秋节吃。中秋节在每年九月或十月，月亮最圆最亮的时候。月饼的做法是：外皮用面粉、糖和油做成，里面包馅儿，传统馅儿有莲蓉、豆沙和五仁，有的中间还有咸蛋黄。用模具压出形状后烤制。月饼的圆形代表圆满和团圆，中秋节那天月亮也是圆的，吃圆月饼看圆月象征着家人团聚。此外，还有嫦娥奔月的传说，人们吃月饼也是为了纪念这个故事。家人朋友之间互送月饼表达美好的祝愿。所以月饼在中秋节必不可少。
topics.sample_en: I want to talk about a food that people eat on a special occasion. That food is mooncake, eaten during the Mid-Autumn Festival. The Mid-Autumn Festival happens in September or October every year. It is a time when the moon is the fullest and brightest. Families gather to enjoy the moon and eat mooncakes together. Mooncakes are made in a special way. The outside is a thin crust made of flour, sugar, and oil. The inside is the filling. Traditional fillings include lotus seed paste, red bean paste, and five kernels. Some mooncakes also have a salted egg yolk in the center. To make a mooncake, you wrap the filling in the crust, put it in a wooden mold to shape it, and then bake it in the oven. The top of the mooncake usually has a pattern or Chinese characters. People eat mooncakes on the Mid-Autumn Festival for a few reasons. First, the round shape of the mooncake represents completeness and togetherness. The moon is also round on this night. Eating round mooncakes while looking at the round moon symbolizes family reunion. Second, there is a famous legend about Chang'e flying to the moon. People eat mooncakes to remember this story. Third, families give mooncakes as gifts to relatives and friends to express good wishes. That is why mooncakes are so important for this festival.

p3_questions.question: Are there any differences between the food people eat today and the food people ate in the past?
p3_questions.answer: Yes, there are big differences. In the past, people ate mostly seasonal and local food. If it was winter, they ate vegetables stored from autumn. If a fruit did not grow in their region, they never tasted it. Today, thanks to modern transportation and greenhouses, you can eat almost any food at any time of the year. You can have watermelon in winter and strawberries in summer. Also, in the past, people preserved food through salting, drying, or pickling because there were no refrigerators. Today, most people have refrigerators and freezers, so fresh food lasts much longer. Food is much more diverse and available year- round now.

p3_questions.question: What are the differences between everyday fooo and festival food?
p3_questions.answer: Another difference is the social aspect. Everyday food is often eaten alone or with immediate family. You might eat breakfast quickly before work or eat lunch at your desk. Festival food is almost always shared with others. It is eaten at gatherings with extended family, friends, or neighbors. Also, festival food has symbolic meanings, while everyday food does not. For example, noodles represent long life on birthdays, but an ordinary bowl of noodles on a Tuesday is just noodles. Lastly, festival food is often presented more beautifully. It might be arranged on special plates or wrapped in decorative boxes. Everyday food is served in regular bowls without special presentation.

p3_questions.question: Why are there special foods on special occasions or events?
p3_questions.answer: Another reason is that special foods create a sense of scarcity and anticipation. If you could eat mooncakes every day, they would not feel special anymore. Because they are only available once a year, people look forward to them. This anticipation makes the occasion more exciting. Also, making special foods often involves extra time and effort. Families work together to make dumplings for New Year or wrap zongzi for Dragon Boat Festival. This shared labor becomes part of the celebration. The effort put into making the food shows that the occasion matters. The food becomes a reward for that effort.

topics.name_zh: 擅长学习和说语言的人
topics.cue_prompt: Describe a person who is good at learning andspeaking new languages
you_should_say: How you got to know him/her
How he/she learns a new language
And explain how you feel about him/her
topics.summary_zh: 俄罗斯室友Alex，会俄语、英语、中文，还会德语和西班牙语。他学中文的方法很特别——听郭德纲的相声，记下所有生词造句子。还看无字幕国产剧，录自己说话对比发音。不怕犯错，主动和中国人聊天。我特别佩服他，不是天才但极度自律。他让我意识到自己对自己的语言太习以为常。他很谦虚，总说“还差得远”。他是语言学习者的榜样。
topics.sample_en: I’d like to talk about my university roommate, Alex, a Russian exchange student from Moscow. I got to know him last year when we were assigned to the same dorm room. At first, I was worried about the language barrier, but Alex speaks incredible Chinese. What languages can he speak? He is fluent in Russian, English, Chinese, and can also get by in German and Spanish. He’s not a genius – he just works very hard. His Chinese is especially good. He knows many slang words that even some Chinese students don’t know. How does he learn a new language? His method is unusual – he listens to crosstalk, which is traditional Chinese comedic dialogue. He spends hours listening to performers like Guo Degang. He writes down every word he doesn’t know, then makes sentences with them. He also watches Chinese TV dramas without subtitles. He told me that he never studies from textbooks because textbooks are boring. Instead, he imitates real people. He records himself speaking and compares it to native speakers. He also forces himself to talk to Chinese people even when he makes mistakes. He says, “Mistakes are how you learn.”. How do I feel about him? I admire him greatly. He has no special talent – he’s just very disciplined and not afraid of looking stupid. Watching him learn Chinese made me realize that I take my own language for granted. He has inspired me to try learning a second language myself. Also, he’s very humble. When people compliment his Chinese, he just says, “I still have a long way to go.” I think he’s a role model for language learners.

p3_questions.question: Why is it easier for children to learn new things than for adults?
p3_questions.answer: Children tend to learn new things more easily than adults due to a combination of neurological, psychological, and environmental factors. Neuroplasticity is higher in childhood, meaning their brains can form new connections more quickly, especially for language and sounds. Psychologically, children are less afraid of making errors and more willing to experiment, whereas adults often suffer from a fear of failure or embarrassment. Children also have fewer responsibilities and more time for unstructured play and repetition, which are natural learning methods. Adults, in contrast, often rely on analytical thinking, which can interfere with intuitive learning. Additionally, children are usually immersed in supportive environments where learning is encouraged and mistakes are accepted, giving them a significant advantage.

p3_questions.question: How do people learn new things?
p3_questions.answer: People acquire new knowledge and skills through various methods. Formal learning happens in schools, universities, or training courses with structured curricula and teachers. Informal learning includes reading books, watching tutorials, listening to podcasts, or using educational apps like Duolingo or Coursera. Social learning is also common — people learn by observing others, asking questions, or discussing in groups. Experiential learning, or learning by doing, is particularly effective for practical skills like driving or coding, where trial and error plays a key role. In the digital age, many people use short videos on platforms like Douyin or Bilibili for quick, visual instructions. The most effective approach often combines multiple methods, tailored to the learner's goals, learning style, and available time.

p3_questions.question: Do people learn any languages other than English?
